--- CRITICAL FINDINGS ---

[CDN-1] R2 images bypass Cloudflare variants
File: src/lib/cloudflare-images.ts (L1-L260)
Evidence: getCloudflareImageUrl explicitly returns R2 URLs unchanged and logs "R2 URL detected, migration needed"; cloudflareImageLoader also returns R2 URLs as-is so no Cloudflare variant/transform is applied. This means images kept on R2 will be served in original form from the R2/public URL rather than as CDN-optimized variants.  
Impact: High-traffic image requests will hit origin/R2 without edge resizing, format conversion, or cached variants, exhausting origin bandwidth/storage read throughput and causing slow page loads.  
Fix: Serve images via Cloudflare Images (or front R2 with Cloudflare image transforms) and change the loader to return imagedelivery.net variant URLs or rewrite URLs at origin to Cloudflare variants.

[CDN-2] Product page is fully client-side and fetches APIs
File: src/app/product/[slug]/page.tsx (L1-L40)
Evidence: file begins with "use client" and the page fetches product data from /api/products via client-side fetch/useEffect (getProduct), causing each page view to issue origin API calls and download the entire client bundle.  
Impact: Every product view generates origin API traffic and large JS downloads, rapidly amplifying origin CPU/bandwidth and causing CDN cache opportunities to be missed under concurrency.  
Fix: Convert the page to a server component or use Next.js server-side fetching/ISR (and hydrate minimal client subcomponents) so HTML/JSON can be cached at the edge.

--- WARNING FINDINGS ---

[CDN-3] Raw videos and large media in /public
File: public/wpvideo.mp4, public/video.mp4, public/Order Complete.webm (static assets)
Evidence: Multiple raw video files live in public/ and will be served as full files to clients (no adaptive streaming, no transforms).  
Impact: Video downloads will consume large amounts of origin bandwidth and can saturate egress quickly with many concurrent viewers.  
Fix: Move videos to a CDN or object storage behind a CDN with streaming/bitrate adaptation, serve low-res poster thumbnails, and lazy-load/route video playback through optimized endpoints.

[CDN-4] User API cache set to private; public APIs lack CDN TTLs
File: src/app/api/cart/route.ts (L1-L220)
Evidence: Cart GET sets headers: 'Cache-Control: private, max-age=60' and ETag, preventing CDN shared caching; most API routes do not set s-maxage or stale-while-revalidate.  
Impact: CDN cache hit ratio will be low for public product data and even small TTLs force repeated origin fetches, increasing origin load under traffic bursts.  
Fix: Use s-maxage/stale-while-revalidate for public product/list endpoints (keep private for per-user data), and add CDN-friendly headers for cacheable routes.

[CDN-5] Many pages/components are client-heavy (bundle bloat)
File: src/components/product-showcase.tsx (L1-L30) and multiple "use client" pages
Evidence: ProductShowcase and the main product page are client components that fetch data client-side and import UI/interaction libs, bundling large JS to every user.  
Impact: Larger client bundles increase per-user download bandwidth and slow TTI, multiplying bandwidth needs at scale and worsening origin/edge pressure.  
Fix: Move data fetching to server components, split interactive parts into small client-only chunks, and use dynamic import/code-splitting for heavy libraries.

--- INFO ---

[CDN-6] Image domains + loader configured in next.config
File: next.config.ts (L1-L120)
Evidence: next.config.ts lists imagedelivery.net, R2 domains and domains array and contains a comment about Vercel optimization; repo also contains a custom cloudflareImageLoader.
